newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Hanson urges more aid for North Korea.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Hanson urges more aid for North Korea.

text.p: Australian rightist Pauline Hanson underwent an apparent change of heart on foreign aid on Friday, calling on Australia to boost its assistance for starving children in Stalinist North Korea.

Hanson, who has built a national following with a campaign against immigration, welfare and foreign aid, said Australia's A$2.9 million (US$2.2 million) contribution to the U.N. World Food Program relief fund for North Korea was inadequate.
"If we seriously regard ourselves as a nation of the Asia-Pacific region, it is incumbent upon us to respond to the humanitarian crisis facing North Korea," Hanson said in a statement.
She said Australia should direct aid agency AusAID to gather rice and grain from Australian producers and should take a leading role in ending North Korea's acute food shortage.

Independent MP Hanson said in her maiden speech in parliament last year that Australia should stop foreign aid and instead use the money to create jobs. She also called for a halt to Asian immigration and attacked Aboriginal welfare programmes.

The World Food Program on Wednesday launched an appeal for an additional US$46 million in food aid to boost the supplies the United Nations is sending for some 2.6 million infants in North Korea, where crops have been destroyed by floods the last two years.
